title: MicroCT Inspection Protocol for Gallium Particle Accelerator Targets
author: Muofhe Tshibalanganda
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.ychfst6

steps.title: Prepare and Load Sample
steps.instruction: Mount the sample on foam (e.g., florist oasis) using prestik at the top, angling it towards the flat side by up to 10 degrees to reduce penetration artefacts.

substeps.instruction: Mark the top of the disk with a small ball of prestik to serve as an orientation reference for checking second scan rotation by 90 degrees.

steps.title: Configure MicroCT Scan
steps.instruction: Perform the scan using a General Electric VTomex L240 system (or similar) with the following parameters:

steps.title: Reconstruct 3D Data
steps.instruction: Reconstruct the 3D data using General Electric Datos 2.2.

substeps.instruction: Apply a beam hardening correction value of 9.3 to reduce artefacts.

steps.title: Analyze and Process 3D Data
steps.instruction: Analyze the data using Volume Graphics VGSTUDIO MAX 3.2.

substeps.instruction: Register the sample using simple registration to turn the sample upright in the software windows.
Perform de-noising using Adaptive Gauss filters with a smoothing factor of 2, edge threshold of 0.2, and 3 iterations.

steps.title: Generate Visualization Videos
steps.instruction: Create .wmv videos of the front and rotation slices.

substeps.instruction: Set front slice to 5mm per slice.
Set rotational slice to 0.1 degree per slice.
Start rotation videos from west (anticlockwise), with the capsule facing up and welded plate facing down.
Name files according to the format: 'Batch # Target # Front slice', 'Batch # Target # Front slice 90 degree rotation', 'Batch # Target # Rotation', and 'Batch # Target # Rotation 90 degree rotation'.

steps.title: Save and Export Data
steps.instruction: Save the filtered data set as an image stack (tiff).

substeps.instruction: Ensure the analyzed volume is saved in a format compatible with free myVGL software.
